title: The Growth Kinetic and Ultra High Hardness of CoCrFeNiTi High–Entropy Alloy by Mechanical Alloying and Spark Plasma Sintering

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Elemental Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, and Ti powders used as feedstock for high-entropy alloy fabrication.
recollection.intervention: Guess: Mechanical alloying of the elemental powders, followed by spark plasma sintering to consolidate the alloy.
recollection.structure: Guess: A predominantly single-phase or dual-phase high-entropy alloy with potential minor secondary phases, likely a BCC or FCC matrix with possible nano- or intermetallic precipitates.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Mechanical alloying promotes uniform mixing and refinement of powders; rapid sintering by SPS aids densification and suppresses grain growth, leading to an ultrafine-grained or nanocrystalline microstructure with increased dislocation density.
recollection.results: Guess: The material demonstrated very high hardness (possibly exceeding 900 HV or around 12 GPa). The refinement driven by mechanical alloying and rapid sintering, combined with the high-entropy effect, led to superior mechanical properties.

score.note: The intervention merely restates the title without milling times, atmosphere, or SPS conditions. The structure is tentative but broadly recognizes a nanocrystalline FCC/BCC-type microstructure, without the specific 83% FCC/17% BCC ratio or <48 nm grain size. The mechanism correctly identifies milling-induced refinement/dislocation buildup and SPS-driven densification with suppressed grain growth. The hardness estimate (>900 HV or ~12 GPa) is substantially above the actual 675 HV, and the strength values are omitted.
